:::{#rem-limits-two-meanings}
#### Two meanings of "limit"

The lower and upper limits of a sum or integral (@def-lower-upper-limits)
are not limits in the calculus sense,
such as the [limit of a function](calculus.qmd#def-limit)
or the [limit of a sequence](algebra.qmd#def-sequence-limit).
They are the ends of the values the index or variable runs over.
The two meanings meet in an integral such as $\int_0^{\infty} f(x)\,dx$,
which means $\lim_{b \to \infty} \int_0^b f(x)\,dx$:
the upper limit $b$ is sent to infinity by a calculus limit.

:::
